task: For the 5 most-open anomalies (ranked from Phase-2 anomaly_status.json), propose a SPECIFIC, NOVEL, TESTABLE explanatory mechanism ('dark matter' hypothesis) for the measurement-vs-prediction discrepancy, distinct from existing recorded explanations.

candidates.anomaly: ANOM_08 — LLMs Know More Than They Show: Internal Truth-Encoding vs. External Hallucination
candidates.measurement: Linear probes on hidden states predict whether an LLM output will be a hallucination with well-above-chance accuracy, with truthfulness signal concentrated at specific answer tokens — yet the model still emits the wrong answer despite internally encoding (a signal correlated with) the correct one.
candidates.prediction: Standard hallucination theory assumes erroneous outputs arise from ABSENCE of correct information in the representation; if a model 'knows' the answer it should output it. So internal-encoding-of-correct and external-correct should coincide.
candidates.discrepancy: A measurable internal/external gap: the correct-answer signal is decodable from hidden states on exactly the cases the model gets wrong, so the failure is at the read-out/selection stage, not the knowledge stage.
existing_explanations: Orgad/Belinkov: hidden states genuinely encode truthfulness concentrated at answer tokens; misalignment is real and exploitable; but probes are skill-specific and do not transfer across datasets (proposed-contested).
Counter (arXiv:2510.09033): internal states mainly reflect KNOWLEDGE-RECALL, not truthfulness; probe success is a recall confound (proposed-contested).
Counter (arXiv:2510.11905): truthfulness representations are BRITTLE, rely on superficial resemblance, degrade under presentation changes (proposed-contested).

(Adjacent literature found in search, also to be avoided) ITI / truth-direction steering; 'commitment ratio' inter-layer disagreement; prior-token-copying attention heads; RLHF penalizing 'I don't know'.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: FREQUENCY-PRIOR OVERRIDE WITH A DECODABLE-BUT-UNROUTED ANSWER. The mechanism is a quantitative competition at the unembedding between (a) a context-conditional factual signal that is present in the residual stream (hence probe-decodable) but is NOT routed to the final logits with enough margin, and (b) a marginal unigram/co-occurrence 'fluency prior' whose logit contribution scales with the log-frequency of candidate continuations in pretraining. Concretely: the model outputs argmax over logits = factual_signal + alpha * log p_pretrain(token). When the TRUE answer token is rare (high pretraining surprisal) and a FALSE-but-frequent distractor shares the local context, the frequency term wins the argmax even though the factual direction (recoverable by the probe from an intermediate layer) points at the true token. The gap is therefore predicted to be a monotone function of the surprisal rank-gap between the true answer and the most-frequent plausible distractor, NOT a function of 'how truthful the model is'.
candidates.why_distinct_from_existing: Existing accounts argue about WHAT the internal signal IS (truthfulness vs knowledge-recall vs brittle artifact). This mechanism is agnostic to that ontology and instead names a SPECIFIC, measurable CAUSE of the routing failure: a frequency/fluency prior at the unembedding with a quantifiable weight alpha, predicting WHICH known-but-wrong cases occur (those with large true-vs-distractor pretraining-frequency gaps). It converts the qualitative 'they suppress correct answers' into a quantitative selection rule with a measurable knob (alpha) and a measurable predictor (corpus frequency rank), which none of the three recorded explanations provides.
candidates.testable_prediction: EXPERIMENT: On a factual QA set, for each item compute (i) probe-recovered correct-answer signal at the layer of maximal probe accuracy, and (ii) the pretraining (or proxy n-gram) log-frequency of the true answer token vs the model's actually-emitted wrong token. PREDICTION 1: among items where the probe says 'correct answer is internally present', the probability the model nonetheless emits the wrong answer rises monotonically with the frequency advantage of the distractor over the true token, and is ~0 when the true token is the more frequent one. PREDICTION 2 (causal): subtract alpha_hat * log p_pretrain(token) from the final logits (estimate alpha_hat by regressing logit residuals on log-frequency) and re-decode; this 'frequency-debiased decoding' should recover the probe-identified correct answer on a predictable majority (>50%) of exactly the high-frequency-distractor cases, WITHOUT any probe-derived label, and should NOT help on cases where the true token already had the frequency advantage. FALSIFIED if the known-but-wrong rate is independent of the true-vs-distractor frequency gap, or if frequency-debiased decoding fails to selectively fix the high-gap cases.
candidates.why_unexplained_so_far: The field split into a probe-INTERPRETATION debate (is the signal truth or recall?) and a separate decoding-intervention literature (truth-direction steering, contrastive decoding) that uses probe/contrast labels to fix outputs. Nobody (per the searches run) closed the loop by predicting the SPECIFIC set of known-but-wrong errors from an EXTERNAL, label-free corpus-frequency statistic and showing a frequency-only (probe-free) edit reproduces the probe-guided correction on exactly that set. The confound debate distracted from the simpler quantitative selection-rule question.
candidates.primary_quote: discrepancy between LLMs' internal encoding and external behavior: they may encode the correct answer, yet consistently generate an incorrect one
candidates.reasoning_trace: Anomaly: correct answer is decodable internally but not emitted -> the failure is at logit selection, not knowledge -> what beats the factual direction at the unembedding? a frequency/fluency prior weighted by alpha -> if so, the wrong-output cases are exactly those where a frequent distractor out-scores a rare true token -> testable: known-but-wrong rate should track the true-vs-distractor pretraining-frequency gap, and a frequency-debiased (probe-free) logit edit should selectively fix those cases.

candidates.anomaly: ANOM_03 — Emergent Abilities of LLMs: Sharp Unpredicted Capability Thresholds
candidates.measurement: On certain tasks, LLM performance is near-random across orders of magnitude of compute, then jumps sharply above random at a critical scale; the jump is absent in small models and not predictable by extrapolating small-model scaling curves.
candidates.prediction: Neural scaling laws (Kaplan, Chinchilla) predict smooth power-law improvement; small-model trends should extrapolate to large models.
candidates.discrepancy: Discrete, unpredicted ability jumps vs predicted smooth continuous improvement.
existing_explanations: Schaeffer 'mirage': sharp emergence is a metric artifact (exact-match / discontinuous metrics on per-token error); continuous metrics smooth it (proposed-contested).
Genuine pre-training-loss threshold (Du et al., Fu et al.): sharp transitions persist vs pre-training loss even under continuous metrics (proposed-contested).
Original Wei et al. empirical claim (proposed-contested).
(Adjacent, to avoid) multiplicative sub-skill conjunction P ∝ p^N; induction-head phase change; 'quanta' hypothesis; U-shaped/inverted-U scaling.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: DE-SUPERPOSITION RELEASE OF THE TASK FEATURE. The relevant computation requires a small set of task-specific 'feature directions' (e.g., the operands and carry feature for arithmetic, or the 'compare two entities' feature). Below a critical scale these directions live in SUPERPOSITION, sharing neurons with many other features; cross-feature interference noise on the task direction exceeds the decision margin, so task accuracy is pinned at chance even though the per-token loss (which averages over the whole vocabulary and is dominated by generic language features) improves smoothly. As capacity grows, an implicit-regularization-driven re-allocation gives the task feature a (near-)dedicated, interference-free subspace at a threshold width/loss; at that point the signal-to-interference ratio crosses 1 and accuracy snaps up. Emergence is thus a genuine internal phase change in the GEOMETRY OF REPRESENTATION (a de-superposition event for the specific feature), and is sharp in BOTH discrete and continuous task metrics because the underlying SNR crossing is sharp — but it is INVISIBLE in the aggregate cross-entropy because that loss is dominated by unrelated features.
candidates.why_distinct_from_existing: It is NOT the metric-artifact account (the sharpness is intrinsic to a representational SNR crossing, not to the metric's nonlinearity), and it is NOT merely 'pre-training-loss threshold' (it specifies the MECHANISM behind the threshold — feature de-superposition — and predicts which scale it occurs at from the feature's required capacity and the model's superposition load, rather than just correlating with loss). It also differs from the multiplicative-sub-skill / quanta / induction-head accounts: the order parameter is a measurable per-feature signal-to-interference ratio from sparse autoencoders, not a count of sub-skills, a discrete 'quantum', or a single named circuit.
candidates.testable_prediction: EXPERIMENT: Train a model family; for the emergent task, use a sparse autoencoder (or supervised probe) to track, vs scale, the task feature's dedicated-ness: its reconstruction fidelity and the cross-feature interference (off-target cosine) on the task direction, yielding an SNR = margin / interference. PREDICTION: task accuracy crosses 50% at the SAME scale where SNR crosses ~1, and this crossing is sharp even under a continuous metric. STRONGER CAUSAL TEST: artificially reduce superposition load by widening ONLY the layer hosting the feature, or by adding an auxiliary loss that allocates a reserved subspace to the task feature; this should move the emergence threshold to SMALLER total scale, predictably, without changing aggregate cross-entropy much. CONVERSE: inject controlled interference (project random features onto the task subspace) and emergence should be DELAYED to larger scale. FALSIFIED if accuracy emerges at a scale unrelated to the feature SNR crossing, or if forcing a reserved subspace does not advance the threshold.
candidates.why_unexplained_so_far: The emergence debate is framed almost entirely as 'metric artifact vs real threshold' at the level of LOSS CURVES; sparse-autoencoder / superposition tooling matured separately and has mostly been used for interpretability, not as the ORDER PARAMETER for emergence. Linking a per-feature de-superposition SNR crossing causally to the capability jump (with the width-reservation causal test) has not been established — the two literatures (emergence scaling, superposition) have not been joined with a falsifiable per-feature threshold prediction.
candidates.primary_quote: abilities that are not present in smaller-scale models but are present in large-scale models; thus they cannot be predicted by simply extrapolating the performance improvements on smaller-scale models
candidates.reasoning_trace: Anomaly: task accuracy is flat-then-sharp while loss is smooth -> the task signal must be present but drowned -> superposition interference on the task feature would drown it until capacity frees the feature -> de-superposition is a sharp SNR crossing (sharp in task metric, invisible in aggregate loss) -> testable: emergence scale = SNR-crossing scale; reserving a subspace advances the threshold, injecting interference delays it.

candidates.anomaly: ANOM_06 — The Reversal Curse: Asymmetric Factual Generalization in Autoregressive LLMs
candidates.measurement: LLMs trained on 'A is B' fail at 'B is A' (GPT-4: 79% forward vs 33% reverse on Tom Cruise's mother); reversed-answer likelihood is no higher than a random name — yet the same deduction succeeds when 'A is B' is IN CONTEXT.
candidates.prediction: Symmetric relations should generalize bidirectionally; 'A is B' training should make 'B is A' available.
candidates.discrepancy: Near-chance reverse generalization from training (but not from in-context), violating basic bidirectional deduction.
existing_explanations: Berglund: unidirectional next-token objective only trains P(B|A); reverse not learned (widely-accepted high-level cause).
Zhu et al. 2024: asymmetry in learned weight matrices from training dynamics (proposed-contested).

Lin et al. factual-recall bias; Wang & Sun representation entanglement; 'Identity Bridge' mitigation; 'binding problem' (arXiv:2504.01928); entity-fragmentation / tokenization (arXiv:2601.07347) — to AVOID restating.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: ASYMMETRIC KEY/VALUE ROLE-SLOTTING IN MLP ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY, GATED BY POSITIONAL-ROLE FEATURES. Factual associations are stored in feed-forward layers as key->value lookups (key built from the subject token's residual, value written to predict the object). Crucially, the WRITE happens with the entity occupying the SUBJECT positional/role slot and the READ is keyed by that same role-feature. 'A is B' installs key(A-as-subject)->value(B-as-object). The reverse query 'B is ...' presents B in the SUBJECT role, but no key(B-as-subject) was ever written; the only B-trace is B-as-object embedded INSIDE A's value vector, which is not addressable as a key. Because the role-feature (subject-position vs object-position) is part of the key, the association is direction-locked at the storage-addressing level. In-context reversal works because attention can copy 'A is B' from the prompt and re-bind B into the subject role on the fly, bypassing the parametric key store. The novel, specific claim: the curse lives in the ROLE-GATING of the key, so it should be REMOVABLE by training even a SMALL number of facts with role-symmetric writes (present each fact in both subject-first and object-first surface forms) which installs key(B-as-subject); and the model should then generalize reversal to UNSEEN entities for which only one direction was role-symmetrized in a meta-learned way, because it learns the abstract 'also write the reverse key' operation.
candidates.why_distinct_from_existing: The accepted cause ('directional objective') and Zhu's 'weight asymmetry' describe THAT the reverse is not trained / weights are asymmetric, but not the addressable-memory reason it cannot be RECOVERED. This mechanism localizes the curse to KEY-ADDRESSING gated by a positional/subject-role feature in MLP associative memory (an interpretability-level claim), explaining BOTH the parametric failure AND the in-context success with one structure (key store vs attention re-binding). It differs from binding-problem/entity-fragmentation accounts: those blame multi-token entity representation; this predicts the curse persists for SINGLE-TOKEN entities and is governed by the role-feature, and predicts a specific meta-learning cure (learn-to-write-reverse-keys) that generalizes to unseen entities — a claim entity-fragmentation does not make.
candidates.testable_prediction: EXPERIMENT A (localization): With activation patching, identify the MLP layers whose key is built from the subject-role feature; ablating the subject-position component of the key on forward queries should degrade forward recall, while the reverse query should show NO corresponding key activation for B (confirming no key(B-as-subject) exists). EXPERIMENT B (meta-learning cure, the sharp falsifiable claim): Fine-tune on a TRAINING set of facts each presented in BOTH orders for a subset S of entities, and present a disjoint HELD-OUT set H of facts in ONE order only. PREDICTION: after enough role-symmetric examples in S, reverse accuracy on H (single-token entities, one-direction-only training) rises well above chance, because the model has meta-learned to install reverse keys — even though H was never seen reversed. FALSIFIED if (a) the reverse failure is not accompanied by an absent/role-gated key, or (b) role-symmetric training on S yields NO above-chance reverse transfer to one-direction-only held-out facts H (i.e., the cure does not generalize beyond memorized pairs).
candidates.why_unexplained_so_far: Accepted explanation stops at the objective level ('it just isn't trained'); mitigation work (reverse training, Identity Bridge) shows you can FIX it by adding reversed data but treats that as data augmentation, not as evidence for a meta-learnable key-writing operation that transfers to unseen entities. The associative-memory key/value localization of facts exists (ROME/MEMIT lineage) but has not been connected to the reversal curse as a role-gated-key addressing failure with a transferable meta-learning cure as the discriminating prediction.
candidates.primary_quote: If a model is trained on a sentence of the form "A is B", it will not automatically generalize to the reverse direction "B is A"
candidates.reasoning_trace: Anomaly: reverse fails parametrically but works in-context -> parametric path is a key->value store, in-context path is attention re-binding -> if the key encodes subject-ROLE, B never gets a subject-role key, so reverse is unaddressable -> in-context succeeds by re-binding B into subject role via attention -> testable: no key(B-as-subject) on reverse queries (patching), and meta-learning 'write reverse keys' on some facts should transfer reversal to unseen one-direction-only facts.

candidates.measurement: Transformers on modular arithmetic reach ~perfect TRAIN accuracy in <1,000 steps but VALIDATION stays at chance for ~10^6 steps, then abruptly jumps to perfect generalization, long after overfitting.
candidates.prediction: Classical learning theory: once overfit (train~0 loss, val high), further training without new data/regularization change will not improve generalization; overfitting is a dead end.
candidates.discrepancy: Generalization jumps ~1000x steps AFTER memorization, contradicting 'overfitting is terminal'.
existing_explanations: Norm-driven representational phase transition: weight decay contracts high-norm memorizer to low-norm generalizing circuit; memorize->circuit-formation->cleanup (Nanda; Varma circuit efficiency) (widely-accepted).

(Adjacent 2026 work, to AVOID) spectral-gating / variance-limited phase transition (2603.15492); competing-basins singular learning theory (2603.01192); RMT correlation traps; embedding-layer bilinear-coupling saddle (2505.15624).
candidates.proposed_mechanism: REDUNDANCY-DRIVEN GRADIENT-CONFLICT RELEASE SET BY TRAINING-SET COVERAGE OF THE GROUP STRUCTURE. The generalizing circuit (e.g., the Fourier/representation-multiplication circuit for modular addition) requires CONSISTENT structure across many training pairs; the memorizing solution stores each pair independently. During the long plateau, memorization and the nascent generalizing circuit make CONFLICTING gradient demands on the shared embedding/weights; net progress on the circuit is throttled by the fraction of training updates whose memorization-gradient and structure-gradient are anti-aligned. The duration of the delay is therefore predicted to be governed not primarily by weight-decay strength alone, but by the REDUNDANCY of the training set with respect to the group's algebraic constraints — i.e., how many independent algebraic 'witnesses' (overlapping pairs (a,b),(a,c),(b,c)...) constrain each element. Higher coverage redundancy means the structure-gradient is reinforced across many examples and overrides the per-pair memorization gradient sooner; grokking onset (in steps) should scale roughly INVERSELY with this redundancy, at fixed weight decay. The abrupt jump occurs when the structure-gradient's accumulated agreement crosses the memorizer's, releasing the conflict.
candidates.why_distinct_from_existing: Existing accounts make the order parameter a property of the WEIGHTS/optimizer (norm contraction, lazy->rich, spectral gap, basin variance). This mechanism makes the controlling variable a property of the DATA — the algebraic redundancy/coverage of the training set relative to the task's group structure — and predicts the DELAY DURATION from it, which the Phase-2 note flags as exactly the open sub-question ('no quantitative theory explaining the length of the delay'). It is distinct from spectral-gating/variance and competing-basins (those vary optimizer/noise, not data coverage) and from circuit-efficiency (which explains WHY the circuit is eventually preferred, not how the redundancy of data sets the TIMING).
candidates.testable_prediction: EXPERIMENT: On modular arithmetic, hold model, optimizer, and weight decay FIXED; vary only the training-set composition to change algebraic coverage redundancy R (e.g., dense overlapping triples that mutually constrain elements vs a matched-size set chosen to minimize element co-constraint), measured as average number of independent algebraic relations per element. PREDICTION: grokking onset step T_grok decreases monotonically (approximately as T_grok ~ c / R) as redundancy rises, even though final accuracy and train-accuracy timing are unchanged; AND a direct probe of gradient conflict (cosine between the memorization-loss gradient and the projected structure-circuit gradient on shared parameters) should show the conflict fraction falling faster for high-R sets and crossing zero at T_grok. FALSIFIED if T_grok is insensitive to coverage redundancy at fixed weight decay, or if gradient-conflict does not predict the jump timing.
candidates.why_unexplained_so_far: Grokking work has concentrated on weight-space/optimizer order parameters and on WHY the generalizing solution wins; the literature explicitly admits no quantitative theory for the DELAY LENGTH. A data-side, coverage-redundancy account with a gradient-conflict timing predictor has not been established as the controller of the delay (the 2026 spectral/basin papers manipulate optimizer/noise variance, not algebraic data coverage).
candidates.primary_quote: training accuracy becomes close to perfect at fewer than 1,000 optimization steps, but validation accuracy takes close to 1 million steps to reach that level
candidates.reasoning_trace: Anomaly: long flat val then sudden jump, delay length unexplained -> memorizer and generalizing circuit share weights and conflict in gradient space -> the more redundantly the data constrains the group structure, the faster the structure-gradient overrides memorization -> so delay duration should be set by training-set algebraic coverage, not weight decay alone -> testable: fix everything, vary coverage redundancy R; T_grok ~ c/R, and gradient-conflict fraction predicts the jump.

candidates.anomaly: ANOM_02 — Deep Double Descent: More Data (and Bigger Models) Can Hurt
candidates.measurement: Test error is non-monotone (double descent) in model/data size; in regimes near the interpolation threshold, QUADRUPLING training samples can WORSEN test error.
candidates.prediction: Classical bias-variance: test error decreases monotonically with more data; a single optimal model size, beyond which overfitting hurts.
candidates.discrepancy: Non-monotone test error peaking at the interpolation threshold; more data can hurt there.
existing_explanations: Fine-grained bias-variance decomposition: peak is VARIANCE from label noise + random-feature/init; overparmeterization reduces it via low-norm interpolant ('Double Descent Demystified', Adlam-Pennington, arXiv:2011.03321) (widely-accepted).
Nakkiran unified empirical framing / effective model complexity (widely-accepted).
(Adjacent, to AVOID restating) condition-number / small-Gram-eigenvalue blow-up at interpolation (arXiv:1912.06190); spectral-bias & task-model alignment (Nat. Commun.).
candidates.proposed_mechanism: TARGET-ENERGY CONCENTRATION ON THE SMALLEST-EIGENVALUE (LEAST-CONDITIONED) DIRECTIONS AS THE CONTROLLABLE CAUSE, NOT NOISE LEVEL. The interpolation-threshold variance blow-up is mediated by the near-singular directions of the empirical feature Gram matrix; but the SEVERITY (and even existence) of the peak is governed by HOW MUCH OF THE TARGET FUNCTION'S ENERGY (and of the label NOISE) projects onto those smallest-eigenvalue eigenvectors. The minimum-norm interpolant amplifies error along directions where signal/noise sits on tiny eigenvalues (error contribution ~ projection / eigenvalue). The specific, novel claim is a CONTROLLABILITY one: the peak is not an inevitable function of noise magnitude — it is a function of the ALIGNMENT spectrum between target+noise and the bottom of the data spectrum, which can be engineered. Therefore one can make 'more data hurts' APPEAR or VANISH at FIXED label-noise variance purely by rotating where the signal lives in the data's eigenbasis. This reframes double descent's harmful regime as an alignment phenomenon with a precise dial, going beyond 'it is variance from noise'.
candidates.why_distinct_from_existing: The accepted decomposition attributes the peak to variance from label noise + init and treats it as a consequence of noise magnitude and overparameterization. The condition-number account names the small eigenvalues as the amplifier. This mechanism adds the DISCRIMINATING, controllable variable they do not isolate: the projection of TARGET (and noise) energy onto the bottom eigenvectors, predicting you can toggle the entire 'more-data-hurts' effect at constant noise variance by changing only that alignment. The search explicitly noted the 'anti-aligned task -> no peak' prediction is not stated in the literature; this turns spectral-bias/alignment ideas into a sign-controllable double-descent experiment.
candidates.testable_prediction: EXPERIMENT (random-feature or kernel ridgeless regression, where the Gram spectrum is measurable): Fix label-noise variance and sample-size sweep through the interpolation threshold. Construct two target functions with IDENTICAL noise level: (T_top) energy concentrated on the LARGEST-eigenvalue eigenvectors of the expected feature kernel; (T_bottom) energy concentrated on the SMALLEST-eigenvalue eigenvectors. PREDICTION: T_bottom exhibits a LARGE test-error peak at the threshold and a pronounced 'more-data-hurts' band; T_top exhibits a strongly ATTENUATED or ABSENT peak and monotone improvement — at the SAME noise variance and model family. Quantitatively, peak height should track sum_i (target_proj_i^2 + noise_proj_i^2)/lambda_i over the smallest eigenvalues. FALSIFIED if peak height is invariant to target-energy placement in the eigenbasis at fixed noise (i.e., if only the scalar noise variance matters), which would confirm the existing noise-magnitude account and refute the alignment-control claim.
candidates.why_unexplained_so_far: Double descent is treated as RESOLVED via the noise-variance decomposition and the condition-number/eigenvalue blow-up; spectral-bias/task-model-alignment work studies generalization rates but, per the search, has not been turned into a falsifiable 'place the signal on the bottom eigenvectors to summon the peak, on the top to erase it, at fixed noise' double-descent experiment. The accepted framing's emphasis on NOISE as the variance source obscured the separable, controllable role of target-spectral ALIGNMENT.
candidates.primary_quote: the authors identify certain regimes where increasing (even quadrupling) the number of train samples actually hurts test performance
candidates.reasoning_trace: Anomaly: more data hurts near interpolation -> known amplifier is the small Gram eigenvalues (ill-conditioning) -> error along a direction ~ (signal+noise projection)/eigenvalue, so what matters is WHERE target/noise energy sits in the spectrum -> if target energy is on top eigenvectors the peak should shrink/vanish at the SAME noise -> testable: build T_top vs T_bottom at fixed noise; peak present for T_bottom, absent for T_top; height ~ sum proj^2/lambda over small eigenvalues.

honesty_note: All 9 queries were run with the REAL WebSearch tool (R5); links/snippets recorded are from actually-returned results. The searches were used specifically to CALIBRATE NOVELTY DOWNWARD: the literature in these areas is dense and partially overlaps several of my first-draft ideas, and I lowered self_assessed_novelty accordingly rather than overclaiming. Honest collisions found and accounted for: (ANOM_02) condition-number / small-Gram-eigenvalue blow-up at the interpolation threshold already exists (arXiv:1912.06190) and spectral-bias/task-model alignment exists (Nat. Commun.; arXiv:2206.14255) — so my double-descent mechanism is the LEAST novel (0.4); its only genuinely new element is the FIXED-NOISE, sign-controllable 'place target energy on top vs bottom eigenvectors to erase/summon the peak' experiment, which the search explicitly noted is NOT stated in the literature. (ANOM_03) multiplicative sub-skill conjunction (P∝p^N), the 'quanta' hypothesis, induction-head phase change, and pre-training-loss thresholds all exist; my de-superposition-SNR-crossing-as-order-parameter framing with a width-reservation causal test is a refinement (0.5), not a wholly new idea — superposition itself is well known, the novelty is using a per-FEATURE SAE-measured SNR crossing as the falsifiable emergence order parameter plus the causal subspace-reservation test. (ANOM_06) binding-problem (arXiv:2504.01928) and entity-fragmentation/tokenization (arXiv:2601.07347) accounts of the reversal curse exist; my key/value role-gated-addressing localization plus the META-LEARNED reverse-key-writing transfer-to-unseen-entities prediction is the discriminating novel claim (0.55). (ANOM_01) 2026 spectral-gating / variance-limited and competing-basins accounts exist and are dense; my contribution shifts the order parameter to a DATA-side algebraic coverage redundancy that predicts the DELAY DURATION (the explicitly-open sub-question) via gradient-conflict (0.6). (ANOM_08) ITI/truth-direction steering, inter-layer 'commitment ratio', prior-token-copying heads, and RLHF-penalizes-'I-don't-know' all exist; the frequency/co-occurrence prior as a contributor is also discussed qualitatively — my novel element is the QUANTITATIVE selection rule (logit = factual_signal + alpha*log p_pretrain) predicting WHICH known-but-wrong errors occur from an external label-free frequency statistic, plus a probe-free frequency-debiased decoding that should selectively reproduce the probe-guided fix (0.45). No future-dated or speculative preprint was used as evidence FOR any mechanism; future-dated (2026) arXiv IDs surfaced by the index were used ONLY to AVOID restating existing ideas and to lower novelty self-assessments. Net honest read: none of the five is a guaranteed-new idea; the two I judge MOST LIKELY genuinely novel as STATED FALSIFIABLE EXPERIMENTS are ANOM_01 (data-coverage-redundancy sets grokking delay) and ANOM_06 (role-gated key addressing + meta-learned reverse-key transfer); the two I judge LEAST likely novel (sharper refinements of existing accounts) are ANOM_02 and ANOM_08.
